state.misconception_label: Does not understand that 2n represents an even number

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The relevant rule here is that the sum of two odd numbers is always even. However, in your current work, you incorrectly distributed the 2 when adding 2n and (2m+1). The correct step should be \(2n + (2m + 1) = 2(n + m) + 2\). Remember, 2n represents an even number because it is divisible by 2.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so you're saying 2n is already even because it's got the 2 in front of it? But I'm still confused about why it becomes 2(n + m) + 2 instead of 2(n + m) + 1 - like, where does that extra 2 come from?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You are correct that 2n is already even because it is divisible by 2. The extra 2 in the correct step \(2(n + m) + 2\) comes from the fact that both 2n and (2m+1) are odd numbers, so when you add them together, you get an even number. Keep in mind that odd numbers always have a difference of 2 between them, hence the extra 2 in the sum.

score.justification_pass2: While the teacher attempts to state rules and provide corrective feedback, the explanations contain mathematical errors (claiming 2n and 2m+1 are both odd, saying odd numbers have a difference of 2) and fail to show clear worked steps demonstrating the correct procedure.
